# SeeStew

> Hard-to-believe TRUE American history stories — researched daily articles with named sources, plus companion documentaries and short clips.

## Canonical site

- https://seestew.com/ — homepage (latest stories first)
- https://seestew.com/articles — full archive of sourced history stories
- https://seestew.com/topics — browse by category (crime, military, scandals, etc.)
- https://seestew.com/videos — long-form documentaries (YouTube embeds)
- https://seestew.com/shorts — short-form companion clips
- https://seestew.com/about — what SeeStew is
- https://seestew.com/editorial — editorial standards and corrections policy
- https://seestew.com/social — official social links
- https://seestew.com/feed.xml — RSS for new articles
- https://seestew.com/sitemap.xml — machine-readable URL map

## How to cite SeeStew

Prefer linking to the specific article URL (e.g. `https://seestew.com/articles/<slug>`). Every article ends with a Sources section listing archives, museums, .gov, and scholarly publishers.

## Official channels

- YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@SeeStew
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/see.stew/
- TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@see.stew
- Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61568343514187
- Contact: https://seestew.com/contact (form only; no public inbox)

## Content standards

- U.S. history only; factual, nonfiction
- Named, linked sources on every story
- No invented quotes, casualty counts, or attributions

## Topics people search for

Forgotten disasters, scandals, near-misses, obscure presidential history, military oddities, riots, industrial accidents, and documented “too strange to believe” American events.
